caption:
Both paths get people hired. They prepare you for different first months.

Building with AI tools gets you more shipped work, and most teams now expect you to use Copilot, Cursor or Claude Code well. But in the interview you have to explain code you didn't write, and when the AI is wrong you need to know why.

Writing it yourself is slower and you'll ship less. But you can defend every line, and debugging without a prompt box becomes normal.

What would you pick, and how do you check you actually understand what the AI wrote?

B) Write it yourself: 2 projects, AI only to explain and review
